solutions.check: 28 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), agrees with the 27 answers the paper printed

clue.text: One of three on the river Tweed?

definitions.text: One of three on the river
definitions.meaning: Jerome K. Jerome's Three Men in a Boat follows three friends rowing up the Thames, one of them called by this surname
a famous woven woollen cloth from the Outer Hebrides carries this island's name

explanation.walkthrough: 'the river Tweed' looks like one phrase naming the Border river; split it, and the river is the Thames of Jerome's comic novel while Tweed is the cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a rowing companion in Jerome's novel and to the Hebridean island whose hand-woven cloth is world famous.

clue.text: Import a horse

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: Bringing in a horse from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' looks like bringing in goods; here it is the noun meaning sense or significance.
explanation.definitionFit: The import of something is its total significance, what it comes to.

clue.text: Do boxing manager's work in car

definitions.meaning: a boxing promoter's job is to stage a fight
a small light motor car for short trips

explanation.walkthrough: Split as RUN A BOUT, staging a fight; whole, it is a small car.
explanation.definitionFit: A small car for short trips, and staging a contest in the ring.

clue.text: Fine as punishment

definitions.meaning: ... can mean excellent or brisk, as in a ... new car
smacking a child on the bottom

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a monetary penalty, which sits nicely beside punishment, but it means excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an informal word for excellent and a slapping on the backside given as correction.

clue.text: Content to have a couple of rounds around this course?

definitions.text: Content to have a couple of rounds around this course?

parts.words: Content to have a couple of rounds around this course?
parts.note: golfers play rounds on a course in Kent; read again, a filling sits between two rounds (slices) of bread

explanation.surface: A golfer happy to play two rounds at a particular links.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' and 'course' suggest golf, and Royal St George's is indeed at this Kent town; but the filling between two rounds of bread is the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: The snack is filling held between two slices of bread, and the Kent town of the same name hosts a championship golf links.

clue.text: Heavens above! This is excessive

parts.note: the heavens are the sky
high means up above

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock at something overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or hopes soaring very far up are extreme or inflated.

clue.text: American philosopher, say, regarded as naive

indicators.note: say signals that the philosopher's name is to be heard, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: John Dewey was an American philosopher and educational reformer
eyed means looked at, regarded

explanation.surface: A US thinker who is thought of as innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives DEWY from the sound of DEWEY, the American philosopher John Dewey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sentimental and innocent is credulous, with eyes moist like morning grass.

clue.text: In claim I set out to be hostile

indicators.note: set out suggests the letters are laid out afresh, so these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making a claim intended as hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges the letters of IN CLAIM I.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfriendly and antagonistic, from the Latin for enemy.

clue.text: Scot fighting with Gordon at the front

definitions.text: Scot fighting with Gordon at the front

parts.words: Scot fighting with Gordon at the front
parts.note: the Gordon regiment of the British Army was a famous Scottish infantry unit raised in the north

explanation.surface: A Scottish soldier in battle alongside General Gordon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with Gordon at the front' suggests serving under General Gordon; read again, Gordon comes in front of the regiment's name, the Gordon Highlanders.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier of the Gordon regiment was a man from Scotland's mountainous north.

clue.text: In by around about six, if not four

indicators.note: the clue opens by saying one piece goes in another, here the jumbled letters going inside the word by

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about can mean out of order, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cricket umpire weighing whether a hit was a six or a four.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges AROUND into OUNDAR, which 'In' places inside BY. In cricket a hit reaching the edge of the field scores four, or six if it clears it on the full.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a hit to the field's rope edge scores four runs, or six if it carries over without bouncing.

clue.text: Pledging without minimal sum up front as cover

indicators.note: without means the small sum is dropped from the longer word for pledging, here from its very start

parts.note: pawning goods is pledging them as security for a loan
P stands for a penny, the smallest sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone pawning goods without even a tiny sum paid in advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops P (a penny) from PAWNING; 'up front' says the P goes from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sheet over a shop window or patio is a shelter from sun and rain.

clue.text: Face growth that's limited in August

definitions.meaning: a small pointed tuft of beard grown only under the lower lip, as worn by Napoleon III
august as an adjective means majestic or stately, befitting an emperor

explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective meaning majestic.
explanation.definitionFit: The small chin tuft was named after Napoleon III's beard, and stately grandeur befits an emperor.

clue.text: Reducing one's stature as conquering heroine

definitions.meaning: bending the body forward and down makes a person shorter
Goldsmith's comedy She Stoops to Conquer has Kate Hardcastle lower herself to win her suitor

explanation.walkthrough: Goldsmith's play She Stoops to Conquer has its heroine pose as a barmaid to win the man she loves.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending low lessens one's height, and Goldsmith's heroine lowers herself socially in order to win.

clue.text: Used time recorder

definitions.meaning: pre-owned, not new
the thin pointer on a clock face that sweeps out the seconds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Used time' looks like one phrase; split it after 'Used'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods previously owned are not new, and a clock's seconds pointer records time.

clue.text: Accommodation for one sort of industry

definitions.meaning: a small country house is somewhere to live
small-scale manufacture done at home goes by this word followed by industry

explanation.walkthrough: A home-based craft business is called a cottage industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural dwelling, and the first half of the phrase for home-based craft manufacture.

clue.text: Sound of bell limits a head doing this?

definitions.text: Sound of bell limits a head doing this?

indicators.note: limits means the bell's sound bounds the other piece on either side

parts.note: ting is the light ringing sound of a small bell
each means per head, for every one

explanation.surface: A school bell rings, marking the bounds of the headmaster's lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue pictures a head teacher at work while the school bell marks the lesson's start and end.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving lessons is the work of a head teacher, framed here by the school bell.

clue.text: Suspension of a governor over improper use of cane

parts.note: a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: improper use means the letters of the next word are put to a wrong order

explanation.surface: A governor caning someone wrongly and being suspended for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improper use of' rearranges CANE into ANCE; a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter in abeyance is temporarily on hold, pending a later decision.

clue.text: Solved puzzles full of holes

definitions.meaning: to riddle can mean to solve or explain a riddle
something peppered with bullet holes or worm holes

explanation.walkthrough: The verb riddle has two unrelated senses: to read a riddle, and to pierce all over.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of riddle means both having solved enigmas and perforated throughout.

clue.text: Gain attention

definitions.meaning: money earned on a loan or savings
curiosity or concern given to something

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both money earned on capital and engaged curiosity.

clue.text: One under the influence of pre-Roman roadmaker, according to Chesterton

definitions.meaning: someone under the influence of alcohol is habitually drunk
Chesterton's poem The Rolling English Road says a reeling drinker made the winding road before the Romans came

explanation.walkthrough: Chesterton's poem opens: 'Before the Roman came to Rye ... The rolling English drunkard made the rolling English road.'
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drinker, whom Chesterton's poem credits with laying out England's winding lanes.

clue.text: Unusually gifted youth leader unable to settle

indicators.note: unusually means the word that follows is arranged out of its usual order
a leader is the first, so take the opening letter of youth

explanation.surface: A remarkably talented head of the youth group who cannot keep still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges GIFTED into FIDGET; 'leader' gives the Y of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless and squirming, unable to keep still.

clue.text: Burglar I encountered foolishly turned to run

indicators.note: something done foolishly is done wildly, so the letters of the next word are muddled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A householder meets a burglar and stupidly turns tail to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foolishly' rearranges TURNED into NTRUDE; 'encountered' just links the I to what follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A housebreaker is someone who enters a property without permission.

clue.text: Draw out point legally established

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
licit means lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A lawyer drawing out a point that has been legally settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a response or extract information from someone.

clue.text: Victory started and finished in one

definitions.text: Victory started and finished in one

parts.words: Victory started and finished in one
parts.note: Nelson's flagship HMS Victory was built at Chatham and now rests in Portsmouth's naval shipyard

explanation.surface: A win that began and ended in the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victory' looks like a win but is Nelson's ship, built at Chatham and now preserved at Portsmouth, both naval shipbuilding yards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships are built and repaired at a naval yard, and HMS Victory was launched from one and now lies in another.

clue.text: Dresses and coordinates

definitions.meaning: soldiers dress their ranks by straightening them into line
brings things into agreement or line with each other

explanation.walkthrough: In drill, to dress ranks is to straighten soldiers into line.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean bringing things into straight line or agreement.

clue.text: Can characters in poem show such refinement?

indicators.note: in means the shuffled letters are set inside the word for a mournful poem

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the word can are taken in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A question of whether a word like can belongs in refined verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' gives the letters of CAN as ANC, which 'in' places inside ELEGY.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace and polish of style is a stylish refinement.

clue.text: Scoundrel appears to offend, taken in by constable

parts.note: a dog is a contemptible fellow

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the word for offending sits within the word by

parts.note: taken as written
to err is to sin or offend

explanation.surface: A rogue seems to commit a crime and is arrested by a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogberry is the bumbling constable of Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic watchman in Much Ado About Nothing is a blundering police officer.

clue.text: Put back celebration in gallery until now

indicators.note: in means the turned word is placed inside the gallery's name

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: put back means the word for a celebration is written backwards

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Postponing a party at an art gallery until the present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put back' turns DO, a party, into OD, and 'in' places it inside TATE, the London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so far, up to the present moment.
